- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% above recent low to avoid false optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive declines), reduce forecast slope to avoid lagged momentum.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >5% in early days (e.g., day 1–5), apply a 2–3 day decay correction to smooth out overconfidence.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.3 in 3-day window), reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid sentiment-driven noise amplification.
